notes: BLOCKER-INSURANCE-01. A specific company-name search returns 82,071 total matching agency records -- essentially the entire agency population -- with zero of the top 3 displayed candidates ((HORN) HOUSE OF INSURANCE & BONDS LLC, (MIA) MULTIPLE INSURANCE ASSOCIATE CORPORATION, &PARTNERS LLC) bearing any relation to 'National Trust Insurance Group'. Root cause confirmed by direct code inspection: lib/guided-research/session.ts's insuranceIntent block (createUnscopedGuidedSession) unconditionally sets session.insuranceResearchMode='cohort' whenever session.identifier is unset -- there is NO identity-name extraction path for insurance at all (unlike lender/investor, which at least attempt a 'named X' regex, and unlike move, fixed in R1-016 to use plan.entityName). Direct-call confirmation: createGuidedSession('National Trust Insurance Group') returns {hub:'insurance', insuranceResearchMode:'cohort', entityClass:'agency'} with identityName undefined.

notes: BLOCKER-CROSS-02. Direct insurance-ask-v1 resolves NAIC 10064 correctly to 'CITIZENS PROP INS CORP' (terminalState=RESULTS). Ask parent rejects the identical, specialist-confirmed-valid code as invalid. Root cause confirmed by direct regex testing: lib/guided-research/session.ts's labeledIdentifier regex (`/\b(CRD|NPN|NAIC|NMLS|LEI)\s*#?\s*([A-Z0-9-]+)\b/i`) greedily captures the word immediately after the label instead of skipping filler words -- 'NAIC code 10064'.match(...) yields {type:'NAIC', value:'code'}, silently substituting the literal word 'code' for the real value '10064' before any specialist call is made. This is a request-corruption bug, not a specialist limitation. CONFIRMED TO GENERALIZE beyond NAIC: the same regex produces {type:'NPN',value:'number'} for 'NPN number 20000635', {type:'CRD',value:'number'} for 'CRD number 166089', and {type:'NMLS',value:'number'} for 'NMLS number 3030' -- i.e. this defect structurally affects every identifier family whenever a natural filler word ('number', 'code') appears between the label and the digits, not just NAIC. Only the NAIC case was verified end-to-end against a live specialist in this sweep; the others are confirmed at the regex-parsing level but not re-verified against live specialist responses.
